subject: SLA template — baseline uptime & monthly credit schedule (EmberTech)
messages:
From: Ava Simmons <ava.simmons@embertech.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@embertech.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLAs – baseline uptime + monthly credit ask

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed by the throughput numbers. We're moving toward an internal pilot and need to iron out the operating-levels that will go into procurement. A few asks from our side:

- EmberTech runs large nightly batch jobs; we want an explicit carveout for scheduled batch-induced latency spikes. Can you propose an uptime/latency exception mechanism that won't trigger credits for those windows?
- For the hosted plan, what is your standard monthly uptime percentage (we've seen 99.9% and 99.95 references) and how do you calculate monthly credits when the bar is missed?
- We need a clear cap on monthly credit exposure so our finance team can model spend.

I'm attaching our procurement template and a short list of blackout windows. Can your legal or sales ops team provide a redline of Redwood's standard SLA with those items addressed?

Would appreciate a response by EOD Thurs so we can keep the procurement cycle moving.

Thanks,
Ava Simmons
Director, Platform Partnerships
EmberTech

Attachment: EmberTech_procurement_template.docx (attachment stub)

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Ava Simmons <ava.simmons@embertech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLAs – baseline uptime + monthly credit ask

Hi Ava — thanks for the list and for the quick turnaround. Looping in Laura (Contracts) and Marissa (Sales Ops) to help with the redline and the credit cap discussion.

Quick answers up front:
- Standard hosted baseline: 99.95% monthly availability for the platform control plane and model serving for single-request (interactive) workloads.
- For batch-heavy workloads we typically offer a carveout via an "operational window" definition (scheduled jobs must be registered; unconstrained bursts still count against uptime).
- Monthly credits: calculated on a per-account monthly invoice basis as a percentage of that month's Redwood service charges (not a separate cash payout). We can put a cap (e.g., 50% of that month's service charges) or a hard-dollar cap if that's required.

Action items: Laura — can you review EmberTech's template and produce a redline that includes an operational window definition and two alternate credit cap options (percent cap and absolute cap)? Marissa — can you run a model of expected credit exposure for a mid-sized pilot (projected $45k monthly spend) under both caps?

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_template_v1.1.pdf (attachment stub)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, Ava Simmons <ava.simmons@embertech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLAs – baseline uptime + monthly credit ask

Ava / Connor — see the attached redline (EmberTech_SLA_redline_20250612.pdf). High level summary of changes:

1) Operational Window (section 2.3): added a process for registering scheduled batch windows (minimum 72 hours advanced notice, window start/end times in UTC, and a maximum per-window duration of 8 hours unless pre-approved). Any performance degradation that occurs entirely within a registered window is excluded from uptime calculations.

2) Credit calculation (section 4.1): credits remain applied to the monthly Redwood service invoice and are computed as a percentage of that month's charges that are attributable to affected services. We added a formula example.

3) Credit cap (section 4.3): provided two options — Option A: percent cap of 50% of monthly charges; Option B: absolute-dollar cap equal to 2x the average daily run-rate times 30 (we've included a worked example). We included a fallback that if the parties select Option B, they must provide 3 months of historical usage to set the base run-rate.

4) Maintenance carve-outs: clarified planned maintenance windows must be published 7 days in advance; emergency maintenance (safety/security) has a separate notification practice and limited credit exposure.

Connor / Marissa — please validate the legal language and the numbers; Ava, happy to walk through the redline on a call if helpful.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: EmberTech_SLA_redline_20250612.pdf (attachment stub)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLAs – baseline uptime + monthly credit ask

Folks — ran the exposure model for the $45k pilot:

- Option A (50% percent cap): max credit = $22,500 in a month if the account hits the worst band that triggers full crediting. Realistic historical outages across similar accounts indicate single-month credits > $5k are rare; we've included a 3-scenario waterfall (nominal / stress / severe) in the attached spreadsheet.
- Option B (absolute-dollar cap): under our formula the 2x daily-run-rate cap translates to ~$6,000 monthly for the pilot (we used a 30-day projection). This is more palatable to finance but requires EmberTech to provide 3 months of usage so we can set the base daily run-rate.

Recommendation for pilot: pick Option B (absolute cap) and provide the three months of usage; for ramp to production, move to Option A at a 40% cap with a gradual phase-in.

I'll draft sample contract language that maps the chosen option to invoice mechanics and a monthly reconciliation schedule.

-Marissa Cole
Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: exposure_model_pilot_45k.xlsx (attachment stub)

Connor / Laura / Marissa — thank you for the fast turn. EmberTech's procurement team reviewed the redline and we have two asks before we sign:

1) Reduce the absolute cap in Option B to 1.5x daily run-rate (our CFO is wary of the 2x multiplier for pilots).
2) Add a one-time credit carve-in for the pilot month if outages exceed the stress scenario (>25% of monthly requests impacted) — EmberTech will accept a prorated one-time remediation credit that is outside the monthly cap but only for the pilot month.

If you can accept those two adjustments, we can route the redline to DocuSign early next week. Otherwise, we can take Option A at 40% cap and a 30-day phased cap-down to 25% after three months of stable operation.

Would prefer a short call Monday to finalize.

Best,
Ava
